messages:
lena: FYI opened support case ACME-9924 — customer reports promo tokens applied but usage shows no debits, they ran many chat streams earlier today and saw generated content. attaching their curl sample and request ids.

 tickets-bot: ticket ACME-9924 created · priority P2 · assigned to lena

 lena: short summary — promo grant promo_march_launch auto-applied to acct, also had existing free_trial balance. After multiple streaming chat calls the UI still shows full balances, customer insists responses contained tokens (non-empty content) but ledger has no debit lines.

 lena: curl they used:
 ```
 curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_redwoodxxx" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"please summarize Q1 leads"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
 ```

 lena: customer gave idempotency key idemp_20260301_acme_B and a handful of request ids; they used SDK v0.9.2 over HTTP chunked streaming (Transfer-Encoding: chunked).

 ryan: quick asks from eng-runtime: did they use the streaming /stream endpoint exclusively? need proxy logs for those request ids and billing finalize traces.

 lena: attached proxy excerpt and our intermediate billing hook logs. relevant lines:
 ```
 [proxy] req=req-2a7 path=/v1/chat/stream idemp=idemp_20260301_acme_B
 [billing-hook] enqueue finalize for request=req-2a7
 [proxy] client closed stream, status=200
 ```

 lena: but billing-consumer shows: 
 ```
 billing.consumer: finalize handler: unable to resolve ledger_key for acct=acct_7XyZ -> undefined
 billing.consumer: skipping finalize for req=req-2a7
 ```

 amar: that 'undefined' mapping is suspicious — could be related to the new ledger aliasing we introduced to support promo namespaces. I'll pull ledger rows and event table entries.

 amar: DB snapshot for acct_7XyZ:
 - ledger_balance.default: 0
 - ledger_balance.free_trial: 10000
 - ledger_balance.promo_march_launch: 25000 (granted 2026-03-01T10:05Z)

 amar: billing_events table shows no debit rows for those request_ids in the 09:30-11:15 window. finalize queue had entries but consumer log shows mapping resolved to undefined and then skipped.

 ryan: give me the consumer stack trace around the mapLedger resolution and the billing-consumer commit hash.

 lena: stack snippet:
 ```
 TypeError: Cannot read property 'ledger_id' of undefined
     at mapLedger (/opt/billing/consumer/index.js:138:22)
     at finalizeWorker (/opt/billing/consumer/index.js:228:15)
 ```
 commit noted in container: git rev 8f7c4a (recent aliasing changes).

 amar: i suspect a regression in the alias lookup where new promo ledger entries introduced a nil alias for certain account states. Rolling back the alias change on the billing-consumer to confirm. I'll redeploy previous stable rev 8f6b1d.

 ryan: rolling back now, watch logs for finalize processing for req-2a7.

 (5m later)

 ryan: rollback finished, consumer restarted on rev 8f6b1d. New logs:
 ```
 billing.consumer: finalize processed req=req-2a7 ledger=promo_march_launch debit_tokens=420
 billing.consumer: finalize processed req=req-2a8 ledger=promo_march_launch debit_tokens=380
 ```

 lena: told the customer to refresh and check balances — they just confirmed the UI now shows debits totaling ~3.9k tokens across all recovered requests and matches their observed output. They were pretty stressed but relieved.

 lena: root cause summary for case notes: a regression in ledger-alias lookup introduced in commit 8f7c4a caused mapLedger to return undefined for certain promo-ledger configurations; the consumer skipped finalize events instead of falling back to a default ledger. Impact window approx 2026-03-01T09:15 to 2026-03-01T11:20 UTC for a subset of accounts created/modified during the promo rollout.

 amar: remediation: rollback applied, finalized queue reprocessed which recovered most missed finalizes. Permanent fix: add defensive nil-check in mapLedger, enforce fallback to default ledger_id, add unit tests for alias lookup, and deploy patch BILL-1480.

 amar: operational follow-ups for SRE: add a metric for finalize-mapping-failures and an alert if > 5/hr; add a short-window retry/reprocess pipeline to surface these quickly.

 lena: customer asked if we'll issue a goodwill credit since they saw generated content without debits briefly. suggested 2,000-token goodwill. Amar — can you approve?

 amar: approved 2,000 token goodwill credit. I'll apply a promo_adj and note on the account and close ticket after customer confirms.

 lena: draft reply to customer prepared:
 "Thanks for reporting this — we found a bug in our billing consumer that occasionally prevented promo-funded streaming usage from being recorded. We've reprocessed the finalize queue for your account and your balance now reflects the consumed tokens. We've also issued a 2,000-token goodwill credit for the inconvenience. If anything still looks off please reply and we'll investigate immediately."

 lena: adding internal case note and linking BILL-1480 PR. closing once customer ACKs. :white_check_mark:
